title: Bhai Taru Singh refuses to plead for the Nawab

blocks.text: Bhai Taru Singh responds by laying down a clear principle: he would sacrifice everything for a Sikh, but he will not advocate for a wicked oppressor who has earned a righteous curse. The page stresses that Khalsa Panth alone being empowered to annul that curse does not mean the Panth is obliged to excuse injustice lightly.

Meanwhile the Nawab's treatment fails, and each attempted remedy only worsens his condition. His desperation keeps sending petitions back through intermediaries, but Taru Singh's moral clarity remains intact.
The result is a page about disciplined mercy rather than simple vengeance. The Panth is shown as possessing power over the case, yet also insisting that power must answer to righteousness.
